look_here_first: STOP IDENTIFYING ALL RED-SPOTTED MATS AS EUPHORBIA MACULATA. Begin with small opposite leaves (often RED blotch, not necessary) on a low hairy spreading annual. Under magnification, confirm fine appressed HAIRS ACROSS the whole capsule FACES, not just along keels; E. prostrata has conspicuous hairs mainly on capsule KEELS. Mature E. maculata seeds have a few LOW TRANSVERSE ridges or shallow crosswise wrinkles, not lengthwise ribs; prostrata has STRONG sharp crosswise seed ridges; E. serpens has a GLABROUS capsule and a seed lacking strong ribs. Photograph the node and narrow stipules, but don't claim red spot or mat habit alone proves species. This learner has no completed BONAP county-native decision: county-range metrics stay excluded until reviewed.

morphology_keys.life_cycle: Annual with a taproot; stems usually lie flat and do not root at nodes.
morphology_keys.leaves: Opposite, asymmetric at base, 4–18 × 2.5–8 mm, often red-blotched but variable.
morphology_keys.reproductive: Tiny cup-shaped cyathia in leaf axils; hairy 3-lobed capsules and longitudinally ridged seeds are stronger tie-breakers than leaf color.
best_field_traits: Low annual radiating creeping mat; long stems often prostrate and do not normally root at soil-contact nodes.
Opposite small leaves with unequal/asymmetric bases; minutely toothed margins, sometimes with dark midrib blotch; SPOT MAY BE ABSENT.
Narrow pointed stipules near leaf bases, not broad fused triangular scales of E. serpens.
Fine hairs across stems and leaf surfaces, especially below; also fine APPRESSED hairs evenly distributed over capsule faces.
Three-lobed capsules generally about 1.3–1.5 mm; surface pubescence all over, NOT mainly on raised keel ridges.
Seeds about 1 mm, angular, with a few LOW, INCONSPICUOUS TRANSVERSE ridges/wrinkles. Do NOT describe these as longitudinal ridges.
Fruit hair DISTRIBUTION versus E. prostrata is more immediately useful than dark leaf patches.
morphology_keys.family_pattern: Euphorbiaceae / Euphorbia sect. Anisophyllum. Minute cyathia (cups containing reduced flowers), opposite leaves, three-lobed capsules. Exact species needs fruit and seed morphology.
morphology_keys.seed: Mature seeds oblong-ovoid, sharply angular, about 1–1.2 by 0.6–0.9 mm; FNA describes 3–4 low transverse ridges crossing angles, unlike stronger narrow cross-ribs on E. prostrata. Older project note describing lengthwise ridges was incorrect and is superseded.
morphology_keys.fruit: Fruit three-lobed and exserted, around 1.3–1.5 mm, fine appressed hairs scattered relatively evenly across the rounded faces. Unlike E. prostrata, which has more projecting or crisped hairs concentrated along keels.
morphology_keys.leaf_base: Leaf bases strongly asymmetric with one side more truncate and sometimes forming a rounded lobe/auricle. Photo of whole habit may not resolve it; a sharp close-up and orientation of single entire paired leaves is best.
crew_field_photography: 1. Photograph entire mat and opposite leaves; record both spotted and spotless leaves.
2. Get macro of paired leaf BASES at one node; include a 1 mm reference, check asymmetry and narrow stipules.
3. Find real THREE-LOBED CAPSULE, use 10× or stronger; look for pale tiny hairs across the middle of its FACE, not just projecting from edges.
4. Photograph mature released seeds with 1–2 mm scale, rotate seed, look for LOW CROSSWISE grooves. Compare to strongly ridged prostrata seed.
5. If only red spots or low mat habit photographed, label sandmat Euphorbia sp. until capsules/seeds can be documented.
morphology_keys.crew_lesson: Look at the fruit, not the spot! Maculata has fine hairs ALL OVER the capsule; prostrata is fuzzy along the edges/keels; serpens is bald. Maculata seeds have subtle crosswise wrinkles, prostrata seeds have bold crosswise ribs, serpens seeds look smooth.
morphology_keys.habitat_and_safety: Frequent in disturbed soil, cracks, lawn and path edges. Native to North America, but exact Hays county target approval must be checked with BONAP and is NOT assumed here. Milky latex may irritate skin/eyes; avoid unnecessary stem rupture.

comparisons.key_distinctions: E. MACULATA has appressed hair spread across capsule faces and a few SHALLOW CROSSWISE seed furrows. E. PROSTRATA has longer crisped hair mainly on KEELS and strong sharp TRANSVERSE seed ridges. E. SERPENS has glabrous capsules, smooth seeds and broad fused stipule scales, often rooting at soil-contact nodes. Leaf spots alone are never sufficient.
comparisons.photo_tie_breakers: Four properly credited exact-species files now installed: whole mat, narrow stipule/hairy node, appressed capsule FACE hairs, and LOW transverse seed furrows. Older noncommercial photo is withheld from strict public distribution.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Spotted spurge: the capsule hair LOCATION makes the call
steps: Look at the 3-lobed fruit: is it hairy ACROSS the rounded capsule faces? That strongly supports E. maculata.
Compare the E. prostrata photo, where projecting hairs concentrate along keel edges. E. serpens has a hairless capsule.
See maculata's mature seed: it has SHALLOW CROSSWISE furrows, not strong ridges like prostrata.
Look back to the leaf node for narrow pointed stipules and hairy stems. The red spot is just a supporting clue.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: Tiny appressed hairs across the WHOLE capsule + a few shallow transverse seed ridges = E. maculata. Red center spots alone are insufficient.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: The original seed note in this project incorrectly said LONGITUDINAL ridges; corrected to FNA LOW TRANSVERSE ridges. Four new photos are from Australia/Austria, not local Hays County evidence.
